cohort: The study included 1676 singleton natural pregnancy cases (343 spontaneous preterm birth, 144 iatrogenic preterm birth, and 1189 full-term controls) collected from the International Peace Maternity & Child Health Hospital of Shanghai.
finding: The risk factors for spontaneous preterm birth and iatrogenic preterm birth are distinct, with iatrogenic preterm birth being associated with a higher incidence of worse pregnancy outcomes, including lower birth weight, length, and 1-minute Apgar score, compared to spontaneous preterm birth.
